raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Since #45925, the DSpark draft batch carries no host sequence lengths when the draft attention backend sets `needs_cpu_seq_lens = False`. That is right for `trtllm_mha`, but the DeepSeek-V4 backend also sets it to False under DSpark on CUDA. Its draft-block prep, `init_forward_metadata_dspark_draft_block`, then read the lengths back with `seq_lens.tolist()`, which caused two problems:

- **The metadata glue graph turned off.** The first glue capture of each server fails with `Cannot copy between CPU and CUDA tensors during CUDA graph capture`, and the runner falls back to eager draft metadata prep for the rest of the run:
  ```
  Metadata glue-graph capture failed for key (1, '5', '5'); falling back to eager metadata prep permanently.
  ```
- **A device-to-host sync on every draft step.** From then on, every eager prep calls `seq_lens.tolist()` again.

On CUDA the draft-block prep does not need host lengths at all:

- The extend lengths are `[block_size] * bs`.
- The causal expand runs its Triton kernel from the device tensors and drops the host lists.
- Compression is off for the draft block.

## Modifications

- `compute_uniform_extend_lengths` accepts `seq_lens_cpu=None`. It then takes the batch size from `seq_lens` and returns no host copy of the extended lengths.
- The DeepSeek-V4 draft-block prep passes `None` through instead of calling `seq_lens.tolist()`.
- One CPU test for the helper, with and without host lengths.

## Accuracy Tests

The draft metadata comes from the same device tensors as before. Accept length is unchanged with real drafts: DEP2 with real acceptance gives a median of 2.0 to 2.2 on both arms at every batch size.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

GB300, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DSpark block 5, one node per arm, one run each. Main is `cb55d77d37`, and the fix is the same commit plus this change. sa-bench uses input length 1024. The output length is 4096 for TP4 and 1024 for DEP2. Forward occupancy comes from `SGLANG_ENABLE_METRICS_DEVICE_TIMER=1`.

TP4, EP1, simulated acceptance 3.51:

| Concurrency | Arm | Glue capture failures | Output tok/s | Median ITL (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | Forward occupancy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | main | 4 | 562.0 | 5.91 | 1.69 | 94.3% |
| 1 | fix | 0 | 655.5 | 5.01 | 1.44 | 98.7% |
| 8 | main | 4 | 2,081.6 | 10.08 | 3.25 | 97.6% |
| 8 | fix | 0 | 2,122.2 | 9.29 | 3.04 | 99.2% |

DEP2 with DP attention and MegaMoE, real acceptance:

| Concurrency | Arm | Glue capture failures | Output tok/s | Median ITL (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | main | 2 | 946.7 | 13.68 | 7.10 |
| 8 | fix | 0 | 915.9 | 12.90 | 7.26 |
| 64 | main | 2 | 3,829.6 | 25.64 | 16.17 |
| 64 | fix | 0 | 3,773.8 | 25.12 | 16.19 |

The gain shows where the step is short and host-bound: at TP4 batch 1, output throughput is 17% higher and the median ITL is 15% lower. DEP2 is within run-to-run noise.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
